title: Choose the visual world
question: Your copy is kind and plain-spoken. Your look is a hardcore gym brand. Which world should the whole site live in?

options.label: Public Information
options.lineage: British road signs, 1970s public information posters and Isotype diagrams
options.thesis: Dom posts his numbers like a public notice: one plain fact per sign, readable by anyone in seconds.
options.viewport: A huge red prohibition roundel over a bathroom scale, the headline in tight sentence-case type, a blue sign with the offer, one yellow booking button, and a two-line direction sign that sends nervous beginners and racers to different doors.
options.risk: Without strict type and spacing it reads as a children's or council site instead of a confident one.

raised.raise: The booking action sits alone in deliberate empty space, never crowded by neighbours.
Every figure shows its direction of travel (before, after, change), never a lone value.

options.label: The Programme Card
options.thesis: The whole site is the coloured card a trainer fills in with biro: sets, weights, and the scan numbers week by week.
options.viewport: One pale green card ruled into a grid, the headline typed in capitals, three weeks of scan numbers written in biro with the scale column struck through, and a red stamp.
options.risk: Handwriting and card nostalgia can tip into twee, and a card format fights a long page with pricing and booking.

options.label: The Quiz Spread
options.thesis: Self-selection as a ritual: circle what sounds like you, count the Bs, open the verdict.
options.viewport: A tilted headline asking which one sounds like you, three lettered answers with one circled in pen, a torn halftone photo and a pink verdict box naming a scan, not a scale.
options.risk: Pink and acid green read as teenage, and the collage noise competes with price and booking.
options.case: Holds audience identification: circling an answer is the friendliest way to let a gym-shy beginner and a racer sort themselves. Loses on clarity, since the noise buries the numbers.

options.label: Dark Console
options.case: Fuses into what the site already is, and a nervous beginner reads it as more of the intimidating gym.
options.kept: The primary action alone in deliberate empty space.

options.label: Night Instruments
options.case: Measurement fits, but a glowing black cockpit is a gym brand again and cold to a beginner.

options.label: Dial-up Nightboard
options.case: A tool-culture world with no link to Hertfordshire gym-goers.

options.label: Brine Calendar
options.case: Day-count labels suit weeks of progress, but the subject has no pull for this audience.
options.kept: Every result labelled with its day or week count.

options.label: Gravity Rain Garden
options.case: Beautiful, and nothing in it explains personal training.
options.kept: Colour that carries meaning, not decoration.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A dark hero photo, a big uppercase promise, one gold button and a stats bar: what most personal trainers ship, at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Black ground, huge condensed headline, a gold booking button and a three-number bar under a framed athlete photo.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design, and close to the site you have now.
